title: Quasi-coherent cohomology of Hom from a finite free complex
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $U$ an open subset. Work in sheaves of $\mathcal O_X|_U$-modules on the localized open site over $U$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $E,I$ be cochain complexes indexed by $\mathbf Z$. Suppose there are integers $a,b$ such that $E^i=0$ whenever $i<a$ or $b<i$, and that for every $i$ there is a finite rank $r_i\geq0$ and an isomorphism $E^i\cong(\mathcal O_X|_U)^{\oplus r_i}$. Suppose every cohomology sheaf $H^j(I)$ is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. Then for every integer $n$, the cohomology sheaf $H^n(\mathcal Hom^\bullet(E,I))$ of the ordinary sheaf Hom complex [def-pur-hom-complex] is quasi-coherent. There is no boundedness assumption on $I$.

source.place: Tag 0A6H (2), finite-column calculation; cohomology.tex Tag 08I5, Hom double-complex calculation. Read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A6H and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08I5.

proof.text: Prove by induction on the nonnegative width d of a support interval [a,a+d]. At d=0 the source is supported in one degree, so single_supported_finiteFree_hom_qc proves the assertion. Finite freeness is only needed on the support interval.

At the successor step, take the actual stupid tail T = E.stupidTrunc(embeddingUpIntGE(a+1)). The tail has width d: outside its embedding range its terms are zero, and inside its range stupidTruncXIso identifies them with E. These isomorphisms also preserve the finite-free identifications. Apply the induction hypothesis to T. The established exists_homComplex_stupid_tail_shortExact applied to the identity of I gives a short exact sequence with end terms isomorphic to Hom(single(E^a,a),I) and Hom(T,I), and middle term isomorphic to Hom(E,I). The first end has quasi-coherent cohomology by the one-column lemma, and the other by induction.

Use localized_complex_qc_homology_extension to conclude for the middle term, and transport through the homology functor applied to the arrow-source isomorphism. For arbitrary bounds a,b, set d=(b-a).toNat; support outside [a,a+d] follows from the original bound by integer arithmetic. This also handles b<a and zero support without requiring a separate zero-complex theorem.

    (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens)

      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U)) ℤ)
    (hEbounded : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, i < a ∨ b < i → IsZero (E.X i))
    (hEfree : ∀ i : ℤ, ∃ r : ℕ, Nonempty (E.X i ≅ SheafOfModules.free
      (R := (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U) (ULift.{u} (Fin r))))
    (hI : ∀ i : ℤ, (I.homology i).IsQuasicoherent) (n : ℤ) :
    ((homComplex (R := X.toRingedSpace.sheaf.over U) E I).homology n).IsQuasicoherent
